<sub>[issuer.go](../../issuer.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.MaxIJSONInteger"></a>

### limes.MaxIJSONInteger

```go
const MaxIJSONInteger = jose.MaxIJSONInteger
```

MaxIJSONInteger is the largest integer a token carries: 2^53 − 1, the largest an IEEE 754 double holds exactly. RFC 7493 (I-JSON) §2.2 keeps numbers within it so that every JSON reader — JavaScript's among them — reads the same value; larger amounts travel as decimal strings (Nanos).

<sub>[signer.go](../../signer.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.TokenType"></a>

### limes.TokenType

```go
const TokenType = "at+jwt" //nolint:gosec // G101: a JWT type label, not a credential

```

TokenType is the JWT typ of every capability token: an OAuth 2.0 access token in the JWT profile of RFC 9068, so a resource server or gateway that validates that profile reads it, with the claims the profile requires, client\_id among them. The type does not name the format: limes\_v does, and a verifier reads the claims under the schema it names, strictly, so an at+jwt of another issuer's making is refused before any claim is trusted. What else tells a capability from another access token is its key, whose kid is in limes's namespace (jwks.KeyIDPrefix): never share it with an authorization server that mints at+jwt (docs/adr/0006-one-token-format.md).

Earlier formats, each with a type of its own, are not accepted: limes-cap-v6+jwt, v5, v4 and v3.

<sub>[signer.go](../../signer.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.HasLimesKeyID"></a>

### limes.HasLimesKeyID

```go
func HasLimesKeyID(token string) bool
```

HasLimesKeyID reports whether token is a compact JWT whose header names a kid in limes's namespace (jwks.KeyIDPrefix): the one thing that tells a capability from an identity provider's access token, since both are typed at+jwt (RFC 9068). It reads the header alone, verifies nothing, and is never an authorization decision: a forged token can name any kid. Use it to route a bearer to the verifier that can decide — Verifier.Verify when it answers true, the identity provider's own verifier when it answers false — which then verifies everything. Verifier.Verify refuses a kid outside the namespace before it looks a key up, so an access token routed to it by mistake is refused, never read; a Biscuit, being no JWT, answers false.

<a id="limes.ContextSigner"></a>

### limes.ContextSigner

```go
type ContextSigner interface {
	crypto.Signer
	SignContext(ctx context.Context, rand io.Reader, message []byte, opts crypto.SignerOpts) ([]byte, error)
}
```

ContextSigner is a crypto.Signer that signs under a context, as a key held in a KMS or an HSM does for its call over the network. Signer uses SignContext when its key has it, so a slow or cancelled call is bounded by the request that asked for the token.

<a id="limes.DelegateRequest"></a>

### limes.DelegateRequest

```go
type DelegateRequest struct {
	// Parent is the capability the child narrows, as the verifier accepted
	// it: only Verifier.Verify and Authorize make one.
	Parent VerifiedCapability
	// Subject is who the child authorises; its TenantID defaults to the
	// parent's.
	Subject Principal
	// Audience defaults to the parent's, and must be a subset of it.
	Audience []string
	// Caveats are the child's; see InheritCaveats.
	Caveats Caveats
	// InheritCaveats copies the parent's caveats verbatim and ignores
	// Caveats. It must be asked for: Caveats with no Ops is refused, never
	// read as "inherit", which would replace every other field the caller
	// set — a budget of 2 would become the parent's 25 without a word.
	InheritCaveats bool
	// TTL defaults to IssuerConfig.DefaultTTL, and is cut so the child
	// expires no later than the parent.
	TTL time.Duration
	// NotBefore is raised, when earlier, to the parent's start: its
	// NotBefore, else its IssuedAt.
	NotBefore time.Time
	// ConfirmationJKT binds the child to a key — typically the sub-agent's.
	// Empty keeps the parent's binding, if it has one: a bound parent's
	// child is always bound.
	ConfirmationJKT string
	// ClientID is the OAuth client the child is granted to. Empty: the
	// parent's.
	ClientID string
}
```

DelegateRequest narrows from a parent capability the caller already holds. The issuer enforces narrowing (Narrows) before persisting so a runtime widening attempt fails before any token is emitted.

<a id="limes.IssueRequest"></a>

### limes.IssueRequest

```go
type IssueRequest struct {
	Subject Principal
	// IssuedBy is the principal REQUESTING the capability — an operator for a
	// root issuance, the parent's holder for a delegation. Distinct from
	// Subject, which is who the capability authorises. Its Subject is
	// required — a capability nobody requested cannot be audited — and the
	// rest is recorded as given: an operator need not be a tenant's
	// principal.
	IssuedBy  Principal
	Audience  []string
	Caveats   Caveats
	TTL       time.Duration // 0 → DefaultTTL; must reach the next whole second
	NotBefore time.Time     // zero → valid from issuance, no nbf claim
	// ConfirmationJKT binds the capability to the key with this RFC 7638
	// thumbprint (dpop.Thumbprint); empty issues a bearer capability.
	ConfirmationJKT string
	// ClientID is the OAuth client the capability is granted to
	// (Capability.ClientID): the client of the access token it was exchanged
	// for, or the software the subject runs as. Required.
	ClientID string
	// OnBehalfOf is the principal Subject acts for (Capability.OnBehalfOf),
	// of Subject's tenant; nil when Subject acts for itself.
	OnBehalfOf *Principal
	// Session is the identity provider's session the capability is issued
	// under, such as the OIDC sid of the token it was exchanged for:
	// recorded beside the capability, never a claim, so that every
	// capability of a session can be revoked together (BulkRevoker). Its
	// delegations take it. Empty for none.
	Session string
	// SubjectIssuer is the issuer of the token the subject was authenticated
	// by, such as the iss of the token the capability was exchanged for: the
	// identity provider ClientID and Session were named by. Recorded beside
	// the capability as Session is, never a claim, so a bulk revocation tells
	// two providers' clients and sessions apart (BulkRevoker). Its
	// delegations take it. Empty for none.
	SubjectIssuer string
}
```

IssueRequest is the input shape for Issuer.Issue. Subject (with its TenantID and Subject), IssuedBy, ClientID, Audience and Caveats are required; TTL, NotBefore and ConfirmationJKT are optional, and the issuer fills in ID, IssuedAt, ExpiresAt and Issuer. Caveats are validated (Caveats.Validate) before anything is persisted.

<sub>[issuer.go](../../issuer.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Issuer"></a>

### limes.Issuer

```go
type Issuer struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Issuer mints capabilities, in this order:

 1. Validate the request (caveats sane, parent narrowing if delegated).
 2. Sign the token, then persist the record, and only then return the token.

Signing first means a capability whose token cannot be minted — a signer that fails, or a token past MaxTokenBytes — is never recorded. The token is returned only once its record is written: if the store write fails, the signed token is dropped, so no token leaves the issuer that audit could not find or Revoke, which refuses an id not on record, could not stop.

<sub>[issuer.go](../../issuer.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Issuer.Biscuit"></a>

#### limes.Issuer.Biscuit

```go
func (i *Issuer) Biscuit(ctx context.Context, req BiscuitRequest) (BiscuitResult, error)
```

Biscuit returns the Biscuit form of a capability this issuer issued: the same capability — same ID, caveats, expiry and binding, revoked together with it — in a token its holder can attenuate offline. One copy can also be revoked on its own; see BiscuitRevocationStore.

Like Delegate it takes a VerifiedCapability, so what it signs is what this issuer signed and recorded before, never a value a caller assembled or widened. It refuses one another issuer named, one read from a Biscuit — wrapping a copy again would shed its attenuation and its revocation id; its holder attenuates it instead — and one that has expired or that the store reports revoked.

It needs no OpShare: a copy attenuated from the form allows no more than the capability, which its bearer could hand on as it is, and a copy that sets limits of its own is counted against Caveats.Copies. Delegate, which has the issuer mint a new principal, still requires OpShare.

<sub>[issuer.go](../../issuer.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Issuer.Delegate"></a>

#### limes.Issuer.Delegate

```go
func (i *Issuer) Delegate(ctx context.Context, req DelegateRequest) (IssueResult, error)
```

Delegate mints a child capability narrower than the supplied parent, which the verifier accepted (VerifiedCapability), so its caveats are the ones its token carries. It does not trust it to be current, though: a parent that has expired, or that the store reports revoked (itself or any ancestor), delegates nothing; nor does a Biscuit copy (VerifiedCapability.FromBiscuit), which is ErrInvalidRequest, as Issuer.Biscuit answers it — its holder attenuates it instead. A parent another issuer named is ErrInvalidRequest: this issuer's store holds no record of it, so revoking it there would never reach the child. A child that would have more than MaxDelegationDepth ancestors is ErrDelegationDepthExceeded (403), refused by Store.Insert before it is on record; the parent stays valid. A parent whose caveats do not allow OpShare — the right to delegate — is ErrOpNotAllowed: delegating is the share operation, and a capability granted without it may not have the issuer mint a new principal any part of it.

A child is metered under its parent: every request and charge the child makes also counts against the parent and each ancestor (meter), so one request of the child is one more on the parent's counter as well, and a parent's limits bound everything delegated from it.

```go
func (i *Issuer) Issue(ctx context.Context, req IssueRequest) (IssueResult, error)
```

<sub>[issuer.go](../../issuer.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Issuer.Reissue"></a>

#### limes.Issuer.Reissue

```go
func (i *Issuer) Reissue(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (IssueResult, error)
```

Reissue signs the capability on record under id again, and records nothing: an exchange that issues one capability per subject token hands it out again without keeping its token (ExchangeStore). The claims are the record's, so under the same key the token is the one Issue returned. It refuses an id not on record (ErrNotFound), a capability expired (ErrExpired) or revoked (ErrRevoked), and an issuer whose store reads no record (a RecordReader, as every Store is) with ErrInvalidRequest.

<a id="limes.IssuerConfig"></a>

### limes.IssuerConfig

```go
type IssuerConfig struct {
	// Signer mints tokens (NewSigner), over a key in memory or one held in
	// a KMS or an HSM.
	Signer *Signer

	// Store records what the issuer mints and answers whether a parent is
	// revoked. Any Store is one.
	Store IssuanceStore

	// IssuerName is the value placed in the `iss` claim. Verifiers
	// require this to be in their TrustedIssuers list.
	IssuerName string

	// DefaultTTL caps the lifetime when IssueRequest.TTL is zero.
	// Zero: DefaultIssueTTL, short enough that revocation propagation
	// latency rarely matters. Negative is refused.
	DefaultTTL time.Duration

	// MaxTokenBytes refuses to mint a token longer than this, which a
	// verifier with the same limit (VerifierConfig.MaxTokenBytes) would
	// refuse unread. Zero: DefaultMaxTokenBytes; negative is refused.
	MaxTokenBytes int

	// Now is the clock; tests override.
	Now func() time.Time

	// Biscuit is the form Issuer.Biscuit seals a capability in:
	// github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/biscuit's Form. Nil: Issuer.Biscuit
	// refuses, and this issuer mints JWTs alone.
	Biscuit TokenForm

	// Logger logs everything the issuer does, naming capabilities by id and
	// never logging a token or a key: each token minted at INFO, each
	// request refused at WARN, each call that failed for the server's own
	// reasons — a store or a signer — at ERROR. A Revoker logs the
	// revocations. Nil: slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger

	// Events are called beside the log, for metrics or an audit sink. The
	// zero IssuerEvents calls nothing.
	Events IssuerEvents
}
```

IssuerConfig is the wiring for NewIssuer.

<a id="limes.SealedKey"></a>

### limes.SealedKey

```go
type SealedKey struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

SealedKey is a private key where no formatting reaches it: under any verb, %p included, in JSON and in slog, and wherever it sits — a field of a struct of yours, exported or not — it reads redactedKeyText. A plain key field cannot promise that: fmt walks into a field it cannot call a method on, and under a verb a value does not take. SealKey makes one; the zero SealedKey holds no key. It is a crypto.Signer over the key it holds.

<a id="limes.SealKey"></a>

#### limes.SealKey

```go
func SealKey(key crypto.Signer) SealedKey
```

SealKey seals key: an ed25519.PrivateKey, or a pointer to one, of which it keeps a copy, so clearing or reusing the caller's key after leaves the sealed key whole, or a crypto.Signer over a key held elsewhere. A nil key, or a nil pointer to an ed25519.PrivateKey, gives the zero SealedKey.

<a id="limes.Signer"></a>

### limes.Signer

```go
type Signer struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Signer holds the key an Issuer mints capability tokens with: it encodes a Capability as the token format and signs it with an Ed25519 key, which may be in memory or held in a KMS or an HSM behind crypto.Signer. It signs only for an Issuer (IssuerConfig.Signer). Verifiers pick up the public keys (statically or from a JWKS endpoint) and validate locally — no RPC per request.

<a id="limes.SignerConfig"></a>

### limes.SignerConfig

```go
type SignerConfig struct {
	// KeyID is the kid tokens carry, by which verifiers find the key.
	// Required, in limes's namespace: jwks.KeyIDPrefix, as jwks.KeyID and
	// GenerateKey write it.
	KeyID string
	// Key signs, sealed (SealKey): an ed25519.PrivateKey, or a
	// crypto.Signer over a key held elsewhere — one that also implements
	// ContextSigner is given the request's context. Its public key must be
	// Ed25519. Required.
	Key SealedKey
	// Algorithm is the alg the tokens name. Empty: SigningAlgorithmEd25519,
	// the name RFC 9864 gives the algorithm. SigningAlgorithmEdDSA names it
	// as JOSE libraries that predate RFC 9864 do; the signature is the same,
	// and every verifier of this package reads both.
	Algorithm SigningAlgorithm
}
```

SignerConfig configures a Signer.

<sub>[keyloader.go](../../keyloader.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.GenerateKey"></a>

#### limes.GenerateKey

```go
func GenerateKey() (SigningKey, error)
```

GenerateKey makes a fresh Ed25519 signing key under the kid jwks.KeyID derives for it. It lives only as long as the process unless saved.

<sub>[issuer.go](../../issuer.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.LoadKey"></a>

#### limes.LoadKey

```go
func LoadKey(path string) (SigningKey, error)
```

LoadKey reads the PKCS#8 PEM signing key at path, under the kid jwks.KeyID derives from it; a deployment that names its kids sets SigningKey.KeyID on the result. For a key that lives only as long as the process, GenerateKey; a deployment that may have no key file chooses between the two itself, so a missing mount is never silently a fresh key.
